paper_metadata.title: A CMOS Dual-Switching Power-Supply Modulator with 8% Efficiency Improvement for 20MHz LTE Envelope Tracking RF Power Amplifiers Muhammad Hassan1, Peter M. Asbeck1, Lawrence E. Larson2

figures.label: Fig. 21
figures.caption: Figure 21.3.2 shows the detailed schematic of the new supply modulator. All three amplifiers use 3.3 V stacked devices for reliable operation with a 5.5V power supply. The linear stage output current is scaled down by a 250:1 ratio current mirror M1’-M4’ and then converted into voltage using a trans-impedance amplifier, across which a hysteretic comparator is placed to generate the control signal for the hysteretic switching stage. references.sentence: In this paper, we propose an improved dual-switch topology based on multi-level control, as shown in Fig. 21.3.1, where the first switching amplifier uses large devices, a 1μH inductor, is hysteretically controlled, provides a low-pass response and roughly 60% of the LTE envelope power.
Figure 21.3.2 shows the detailed schematic of the new supply modulator.
A stacked output stage is used with a dynamic biasing for the stacked devices in the output stage, which is achieved using a source follower amplifier Av, as shown in Fig. 21.3.3.

The measured time domain performance of the linear and switching stages for a 20MHz LTE envelope signal with 6.7dB PAPR is shown in Fig. 21.3.4, while Fig. 21.3.5 plots the measured modulator efficiency with respect to the modulator output power.

Therefore, a 13% increase in efficiency is achieved using the supply modulator, while meeting the ACLR requirements with considerable margin as shown in Fig. 21.3.6, which shows the output spectrum along with the ACLR requirements.
The performance summary of the ETPA is also shown in Fig. 21.3.6, while Fig. 21.3.7 shows the micrograph of the test chip.
